author: agent:claude-code
message: autodyne's design as it stands after the five 'close the gaps' milestones: its areas and components with their code, the project-wide rules from CONTRIBUTING.md, the decisions and lessons kept until now in agent memory files, and the open work as todos. (proposal 01a109e4-7ea2-70ee-a825-7a0cd5781282, proposed by agent:claude-code, accepted by user)

text: Performance is the point: every speed claim is a comparative benchmark against the reference library (NumPy / SciPy, rustfft, ndarray, Burn, JAX ...) on the same machine, checking that results agree before timing.

Numerics are tested against known answers: SciPy / NumPy / statsmodels / python-control fixtures (tests/scipy_parity.rs, generated by tests/scipy/gen_fixtures.py), closed forms or measured quantities; 'it runs' is not a test.
Real time: process / render / next_sample never allocate, lock or block (tests/no_alloc.rs).
Layering: a module uses only modules below it in the README's module table; no cycles.

Errors: one error type per module (Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Error), an Invalid(String) variant built with XxxError::invalid, and transparent #[from] variants wrapping lower layers' errors; internal invariants use expect("why").
Every public item is documented (#![warn(missing_docs)]); CI's clippy and rustdoc deny warnings.
Zero copy where data lives: views over external memory (DynView, DLPack, ndarray interop) rather than copies.

name: Core
intent: The array, signal and type machinery every other module builds on.

name: units
intent: Number traits (Float, Real, Integer, Trig, casts), Complex<T>, decibels, and reflection (DType, Reflection).

name: simd
intent: Vectorized kernels on stable Rust (independent accumulators), AVX2 / AVX2+FMA chosen at run time.

name: signal
intent: The core abstraction: any slice, Vec or NdArray is a Signal; NdArray / NdView with NumPy-style broadcasting, strides and reductions; ArrayMath / RealArrayMath shared with flux tracers.

name: dynamic
intent: Runtime-typed arrays and math (DynArray, zero-copy DynView, NumPy promotion rules with every conversion checked, DynProcessor).

name: dlpack
intent: DLPack 1.x export and import: arrays to and from NumPy / PyTorch / JAX / CuPy without copying.

name: interop
intent: Zero-copy conversions with the ndarray crate (feature ndarray).

name: processor
intent: The Processor trait every effect shares; tuples are zero-cost chains, Vec<Box<dyn Processor>> a runtime chain.

name: channels
intent: Planar AudioBuffer, MultiProcessor, PerChannel and Linked (one detector for every channel).

name: params
intent: ParamInfo and Parameterized (ranges, units, scales, smoothing), Smoothed and sample-accurate ParamEvent.

name: Numerics
intent: General-purpose numerics meant to replace and outperform NumPy / SciPy on shared functionality.

name: fft
intent: Fft / RealFft on rustfft / realfft (portable radix-2 / Bluestein without), plans cached per length, next_fast_len.

name: special
intent: Special functions under scipy.special names (gammaln, erf accurate in the tails, ndtr / ndtri, Bessel I0, elliptic).

name: linalg
intent: Linear algebra on NdViews of any strides through faer, plus LAPACK-style algorithms ported to Rust (divide and conquer, dqds, real Schur, matrix equations, expm, polynomials).

name: schur
intent: Real Schur decomposition: faer's Hessenberg from 64 (EISPACK orthes below), EISPACK hqr2 below 200, LAPACK dlaqr0-style aggressive early deflation from 200 with Schur-form reordering (reorder.rs).

name: matrix equations
intent: Sylvester / Lyapunov (Bartels-Stewart), continuous ARE (matrix sign + Newton-Kleinman), discrete ARE (structured doubling + Hewer).

name: systems
intent: LTI systems as scipy.signal / python-control have them: TransferFunction, Zpk, StateSpace, Gramians, lqr, stability margins.

name: ode
intent: solve_ivp: RK45 / RK23 taking SciPy's exact steps, Rosenbrock23 for stiff problems, dense output and events.

name: random
intent: Rng (xoshiro256++, fork / jump) with NumPy's distributions, and random processes (colored noise, Brownian, OU, ARMA).

name: stats
intent: Statistics as NumPy / scipy.stats / statsmodels: quantiles by selection, moments, histograms, cov, ACF / PACF, Yule-Walker, Burg.

name: Signal processing
intent: Filters, spectral analysis, resampling and measurement, scipy.signal-compatible where SciPy has the function.

name: filter
intent: FIR / IIR design and application (Biquad, SOS, filtfilt, remez, firls, IIR design), convolution with automatic method choice.

name: spectral
intent: Windows, periodogram / Welch / STFT / ISTFT / Lomb-Scargle, hilbert, phase-vocoder pitch shifting and time stretching.

name: resample
intent:
Streaming rational Resampler, upfirdn / resample_poly, Oversampled

.

name: analysis
intent: SpectrumAnalyzer, LoudnessMeter (BS.1770 / R128), TruePeak, PitchDetector, OnsetDetector.

name: iq
intent: IQ modulation and demodulation (AM, PM, FM).

name: Audio
intent: Real-time audio processors and synthesis built on Processor and Parameterized.

name: gain
intent: Smoothed Gain, constant-power Panner, StereoWidth.

name: osc
intent: Band-limited oscillators and mip-mapped wavetables.

name: distortion
intent: Waveshaper and Bitcrusher.

name: delay
intent: DelayLine and Echo.

name: dynamics
intent: Envelope follower, compressor, lookahead limiter, gate, transient shaper, multiband compressor.

name: envelope
intent: ADSR as a VCA and a modulation source.

name: modulation
intent: Chorus / flanger (ModulatedDelay) and Phaser.

name: reverb
intent: FDN Reverb and partitioned convolution.

name: synth
intent: MIDI parsing, Voice and Poly (allocation, stealing, MPE).

name: sampler
intent: Samples with loops, key / velocity zones, SamplerVoice.

name: control
intent: LFOs, the modulation matrix (Modulated), transport and note divisions.

name: wav
intent: Dependency-free WAV read / write with sampler metadata.

name: gpu
intent: GpuArray<f32 / f64> kept in GPU memory, CubeCL kernels through wgpu: element-wise, reductions, FIR, matmul, FFTs (feature gpu).

name: flux
intent: Tracing and automatic differentiation front end: code written over Real / ArrayMath runs eagerly or traced, differentiates (vjp / jvp), and emits StableHLO for external compilers; never on the audio thread (feature flux).

name: tracing
intent: Tracer, graphs with complex values, reverse and forward mode, Scan over whole signals with residual-saving or checkpointed gradients, losses (MSE, multi-resolution STFT), optim.

name: emission
intent: Textual StableHLO written for a backend's limits (Emit::for_backend: max_fft, soft_f64, scan_unroll).

name: backends
intent: IREE (CLI tools, CPU / Vulkan / CUDA / ROCm / Metal, .vmfb), PJRT (plugins via the C API, resident arrays), XLA through JAX in its own Python process (the Windows path).

name: in process
intent: Fused interpreter, scalar scans as register programs, and Cranelift machine code (feature jit).

name: Python bindings
intent: autodyne for Python (PyO3 / maturin, a workspace of its own): NumPy-compatible modules (linalg, signal, stats, random, control, integrate, gpu, flux).

name: Plugins
intent: CLAP and VST3 plugins with nice-plug: autodyne-plug (ParamBridge), autodyne-reverb, autodyne-synth; cargo xtask bundles them with their third-party notices.

name: Benchmarks
intent: Comparisons with other libraries, each checking agreement before timing and printing a Markdown table: bench/numpy (NumPy / SciPy), bench/rust (ndarray, Burn, CubeCL), bench/linalg (across languages), bench/flux (JAX, Enzyme, PyTorch, candle).

title: autodyne is a general-purpose numerics library, not only DSP
body: Stated 2026-10-01: a mathematics library for signals, processes and systems meant to replace and outperform NumPy / SciPy; audio DSP and plugins are one application. Differentiators: zero copy everywhere (views over data where it lives) and reflection (runtime dtype, DynArray / DynView). Performance only counts when benchmarked against peers on shared functionality.

title: flux is a front end only
body: Decided in the 2026-10-02 design discussions: trace -> reverse-mode AD over a small primitive set -> StableHLO as textual MLIR. No compiler IR or backends of our own, no melior / C++ bindings (pure Rust build; libloading for PJRT plugins at run time is fine). The real-time path stays monomorphized Rust; flux never touches the audio thread.

title: The Xla backend stays: it is the only XLA path on Windows
body: Removed in d43f12c, restored in ede31b3: jaxlib links XLA's CPU client into its own Python extension (jax_common.dll exports no GetPjrtApi), and no Windows PJRT plugin is published, so JAX in a Python process of its own is the only way to run XLA on Windows. Pjrt stays the pure-Rust path wherever a plugin exists.

title: IREE 3.11's limits on Windows
body: CUDA needs target sm_80 (newer names unknown) and --cuda_async_allocations=false; Vulkan needs a named architecture (ampere) for FFTs and fails FFTs of 128 points or more (built from 64-point ones via Backend::max_fft); no f64 transcendentals on the CPU or Vulkan and a CUDA pow off by 253 ulp (written out of arithmetic via Emit::soft_f64); loops driven from the host (32 steps per iteration via Backend::scan_unroll).

title: Scan unrolling only where loops are host-driven
body: IREE gets 32 scan steps per while iteration (a 4096-sample gradient 13x faster on Vulkan, 2-3x on CPU and CUDA). XLA and PJRT keep 1: on XLA, 8 steps speed the one-pole forward pass up (127 -> 87 us) but slow every gradient 9-12x.

title: Testing PJRT locally
body: The Windows machine has no PJRT plugin; the NixOS WSL distro (not the default: wsl -d NixOS) runs zml's pjrt-artifacts plugins (CPU, and CUDA on the RTX 5070 Ti with NVIDIA 13.3 wheels unpacked beside it, AUTODYNE_PJRT_OPTIONS=preallocate=false). IREE GPUs in the suite: AUTODYNE_IREE_GPU=vulkan=ampere,cuda=sm_80, --test-threads 1.

title: Aggressive early deflation from 200 x 200
body: LAPACK switches at 75 because its sweeps chase many bulges at once in matrix products; with one-bulge sweeps AED pays from about 200 (300: 26 vs 30 ms, 400: 57 vs 71). Result vs SciPy single-threaded: 10 / 50 / 200 at 2.35x / 1.39x / 1.11x, 300 / 400 at about 0.9x.

title: FMA and deferred sweep updates lost on Zen 4
body: FMA in the reflector kernels was slower (Zen 4's FMA units are its multiply units, no gain for this add-heavy mix). Deferring a sweep's off-bulge updates to one register-carried pass, whole-sweep or in groups of four reflectors, was 1.5-2x slower (dependency chains too long for out-of-order execution). Lesson: the left and Schur-vector updates are already at the core's add/multiply throughput; only reducing work (fewer sweeps, multi-bulge level-3 updates) helps.

title: faer 0.24.4's from_row_major_slice_with_stride_mut swaps its strides
body: It builds the view with row stride 1 and column stride `stride`, i.e. column-major. Use the column-major constructor and transpose_mut (schur.rs block_mut); regression test window_updates_write_only_their_blocks.

title: Full benchmark reruns on a shared machine
body: A full bench/numpy/compare.py run while other agent sessions ran swung unrelated rows by up to 50% (rfft 2.6x read as 1.4x). Lesson: re-time suspicious rows in isolation (best of 5, several rounds) before committing a regenerated table, or regenerate on a quiet machine.

title: Schur from 300 x 300: multi-bulge sweeps (LAPACK dlaqr5)
body: schur is about 0.9x scipy.linalg at 300 / 400 (Lyapunov is ahead there). Chase the AED shifts as many small bulges at once, accumulating each window's reflectors and updating off-window parts and the Schur vectors in matrix products.

title: Regenerate bench/numpy/RESULTS.md on a quiet machine
body: The table mixes runs: the Schur / Lyapunov rows are from 2026-10-04, the rest from the earlier quieter run.

waits_on.on: a quiet machine (no other agent sessions running)

title: Decide: build XLA's PJRT CPU plugin for Windows
body: No Windows PJRT plugin is published, so flux reaches XLA on Windows only through JAX in a Python process. Building //xla/pjrt/c:pjrt_c_api_cpu_plugin would give the pure-Rust Pjrt path there.

title: License under the baseline's library combo
body: GPL-3.0-only with the Open Project Exception, or royalty-free for closed source within its conditions, or commercial: render LICENSE.md, LICENSES/ and REUSE.toml (tend baseline render), set the manifests' license expression, replace CLA.md and the CLA Assistant workflow with the combo's inbound terms (MIT-0 + DCO 1.1 sign-off + patent grant), update README and CONTRIBUTING, and make cargo-deny's policy match the combo's dependency rules.
